Application Materials.content:
The Department will only assess complete applications. This means that we must be in receipt of **both references** as well as the **transcript of results, CV and personal statement**. Applicants should keep track of whether their references have been sent and be pro-active in chasing their referees if necessary.
Personal statement guidance:
- The statement should be **no more than 1500 words**, including detail regarding your proposed research area.
- Explain why you are an outstanding candidate, why you are interested in the subject, and describe your academic, professional/work, research experience and interests and reasons for applying to the School of Public Health, Imperial College London.
- Outline the academic/professional trajectory you hope for in the future and explain why the programme and the scholarship are important for this.
- Include a short proposal (**no more than 150 words**) for a public health research project that could realistically be carried out by you over a three month period, including a novel research question and some outline of what you would do.

Interview Requirements.content: Candidates may be invited to participate in an informal online interview in order to assess if the skills and motivations of the candidate are in line with the programme expectations and offering.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Minimum academic requirement: **2:1** in mathematics, statistics, epidemiology or biology, or a medical degree.
- International qualifications: the academic requirement above is for applicants who hold or who are working towards a UK qualification; Imperial also accepts a wide variety of international qualifications.
- China applicants: to be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA etc, applicants should have been awarded a **Bachelor's degree from a Project 211 university with a final overall mark of 80% or better**. Preference is given to candidates with **85% or better**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
All candidates must demonstrate a minimum level of English language proficiency for admission to Imperial. For admission to MSc Health Data Analytics and Machine Learning, you must achieve the **higher university requirement** in the appropriate English language qualification.
You only need to do **one** of the following to meet the requirement:
- Achieve the minimum score in one of the accepted tests or qualifications.
- Show that you are exempt from the English language requirements.
- Pass the Imperial College London Pre-Sessional English Programme (postgraduate students only).
| Test | Higher Level | Validity |
|---|---:|---|
| **Duolingo English Test** | **125 overall, no less than 115 in any integrated subscore** | 2 years |
| **IELTS – Academic** (Test-Centre / UKVI SELT / Online) | **7.0 overall (min. 6.5 in all elements)** | 2 years |
| **LanguageCert Academic** (SELT only) | **75 overall, no less than 70 in any element** | 2 years |
| **Occupational English Test (OET)** | **Grade B / 350 in all elements** | 12 months |
| **Oxford Test of English (OTE) Advanced** | **155 overall, 145 in all components** | 2 years |
| **PTE – Academic** (Test-Centre / UKVI SELT) | **69 overall (min. 62 in all elements)** | 2 years |
| **TOEFL (iBT) & (iBT Paper)** — old scoring | **100 overall (min. 22 in all elements)** | 2 years |
| **TOEFL (iBT)** — new scoring (from 21 Jan 2026) | **5.0 (min. 5.0 in all elements)** | 2 years |
- **Single-sitting rule:** IELTS and TOEFL single-score re-takes are not accepted. Requirements must be met in a single test sitting. TOEFL "My Best Scores" combinations are not considered.
- **TOEFL scoring change:** TOEFL iBT introduced a new 1–6 banded score system (0.5-point increments) on 21 January 2026. Tests taken from this date must meet the new requirements in full; tests taken before this date are accepted under the old requirements (if within two years of the course start date).
- **TOEFL score delivery:** You must email your TOEFL scores to the relevant admissions team. Score reports sent by post will not be processed.
- **Validity:** All scores must be valid at the beginning of your studies at Imperial if your application is successful.
- You may not need to prove your English proficiency if you have completed a qualification equivalent to a UK degree from certain countries.
- If you require a student visa, you must prove your English language proficiency by completing one of the accepted tests and achieving the relevant standard for your course.

Program Overview.content:
Develop a skillset in Statistics, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence to fully exploit complex health data and perform rigorous big data analyses. Analyse and integrate complex and high-dimensional blocks of health data with cutting-edge quantitative methods. Apply your knowledge to extended real-world large scale research projects supervised by leading academics and industry experts.
- Qualification: MSc
- Duration: 1 year
- Start date: September 2026
- Study mode: Full-time
- Delivered by: [School of Public Health](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/medicine/departments/school-public-health/)
- Location: Hammersmith; White City
Broaden your expertise in analysing health data in this Master's course. You will gain expertise in developing, applying and interpreting results from cutting-edge statistical, machine learning, and artificial intelligence approaches for analysing and integrating complex sets of data that are emerging in the health field.
The course is delivered by international experts. They leverage their extensive experience to design materials which better equip you to handle the complexity of real-world health data. Lectures provide rigorous and accessible theoretical background to the advanced methodology. Each lecture is paired with a hands-on session which applies the theoretic concepts to real-world data. This strong technical component will prepare you for a career in health data sciences.
You will apply the cutting-edge skills you gain to unexplored scientific questions with potential real-world impact. Through closely supervised individual and group projects, you will learn how to perform rigorous research to international publication standard. You will be integrated into a world-leading academic or industrial research team for your final project. This capstone project will give you demonstrable experience applying the comprehensive skillset from the course in a role as a data expert.
The course structure includes core modules and a research project. You’ll carry out an extensive individual research project during the third term (4 months full-time research). During this project, you’ll apply advanced techniques you have been taught to real data sets. You’ll be supervised through the process of conceiving, delivering and assessing a high standard scientific publication, with your work assessed by a paper-style report and oral examination.
Teaching and learning methods include lectures and practicals, seminars and technical tutorials, small group tutorials, group work, computing-based practicals, research projects, presentations and peer evaluations, and a virtual learning environment.
You will acquire in-demand hard skills including coding, data analysis, machine learning, and AI, as well as soft skills including problem-solving, communication, teamwork, and the ability to learn and adapt. You will gain a specific skillset relevant to fast-growing industries such as Data Science, Healthcare, Pharmaceutical, Medicine, Life Science and Biotech, and a transferrable skillset in demand in industries such as Finance, Retail, and Energy. The course highlights local employment opportunities in London, described as the leading biotech capital of Europe with over 400 companies and research institutions generating over £11B in revenue.
Course Directors: [Professor Marc Chadeau-Hyam](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/m.chadeau) and [Dr Sabrina Andrade Rodrigues](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/s.andrade-rodrigues).

Curriculum.content:
- **Qualification:** MSc
- **Duration:** 1 year
- **Study mode:** Full-time
- **Start date:** September 2026
- **Location:** Hammersmith; White City
Core modules: **You’ll take all of these core modules.**
- Artificial Intelligence for Health Sciences
- Introduction to Statistical Thinking and Data Analysis
- Principles and Methods of Epidemiology
- Molecular Epidemiology
- Translational Data Science Part 1
- Clinical Data Management
- Machine Learning
- Computational Epidemiology
- Translational Data Science Part 2
Research project: You’ll carry out an extensive individual research project during the third term (**4 months full-time research**). During this project, you’ll apply advanced techniques you have been taught to real data sets. You’ll be supervised through the process of conceiving, delivering and assessing a high standard scientific publication, with your work assessed by a paper-style report and oral examination.
Balance of teaching and learning: Terms 1 and 2 include 30% lectures, practical and seminars, 5% independent study, and 65% research project. Term 3 includes 100% research project.
Teaching and learning methods include lectures and practicals, seminars and technical tutorials, small group tutorials, group work, computing-based practicals, research projects, presentations and peer evaluations, and a virtual learning environment.
Assessment methods include written examinations, oral presentations, online quizzes, short answer essay questions, real case analyses reports, final research paper, research plan, and project journal and log.

Cost of Attendance.content:
Living expenses at university will vary considerably according to your personal circumstances and lifestyle. Imperial estimates London student living costs as:
- Lower range: £292 weekly; £1,264 monthly; £11,375 for 9 months.
- Average range: £397 to £424 weekly; £1,719 to £1,837 monthly; £15,470 to £16,530 for 9 months.
- Upper range: £489 weekly; £2,118 monthly; £19,055 for 9 months.
Below is a rough guide to what you might expect to spend to live in reasonable comfort in London. Tuition fees and study materials are not included.
| Cost | Weekly | Monthly | 9 months | 12 months |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accommodation - College-run | £250 | £1084 | £9,753 | N/A |
| Accommodation - Private sector | £257 | £1114 | £10,023 | £13,364 |
| Food | £71 | £307 | £2,764 | £3,686 |
| Travel (zone 1-2) | £27 | £119 | £1,071 | £1,428 |
| Personal and leisure | £69 | £297 | £2,672 | £3,563 |
| **Totals** | **£417 to £424** | **£1,806 to £1,837** | **£16,250 to £16,530** | **£22,041** |
Figures are rounded to the nearest whole number. Next updates will be published in August 2026.
International students may need up to £1,500 for start-up costs such as accommodation deposits and flights.

Financial Aid.content:
Applications for the School of Public Health scholarships close at **23:59 (BST) on Thursday 30 April 2026** for 2026 entry.
- **The School of Public Health offers a number of scholarships for our postgraduate taught programmes.** For on-campus programmes, including **MSc in Health Data Analytics and Machine Learning**, the scholarship will cover the tuition fees only equal to the cost of a home student.
- **Overseas (including EU) students can be awarded scholarships but will be required to cover the remaining balance of their tuition fees.**
- There are a total of five scholarships for 2025/26 entry, including **one** for the **MSc in Health Data Analytics and Machine Learning**.
- Applications for the School of Public Health scholarships need to be made by a [separate form](https://imperial.eu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_a8BBZRchfOfLxY2), in addition to the full application for admission for the relevant programme of study. Applicants need to have been made an offer for a School of Public Health programme for 2026/27 entry in order to be considered for a scholarship for the same year of entry.
- Applications are invited from candidates from the UK, the EU, Overseas and current Imperial College London students who have the potential to become leaders in their field.
- These awards are open to all students who make an application to the School of Public Health by the deadline for admission to study for a Master's programme, starting in October 2026. These awards can only be given to students who are studying a programme run by the School of Public Health.
- Applications are accepted from talented candidates from across the world for the School of Public Health Scholarships which will cover home tuition fees only.
- The application form will ask applicants to outline why they are in 'need' of the scholarship, including: financial income and family situation; interest and motivation; achievements and awards; and benefits of scholarship.
- Candidates will need to have applied for their programme of choice and be assessed for entry, in line with entry requirements. As part of the scholarship review process, programme teams will review academic potential, personal statement, research experience and publications, and references.
- To be considered for a scholarship, candidates must apply for a place on a Masters programme run by the School of Public Health and complete the School of Public Health's Scholarships [online application form](https://imperial.eu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_a8BBZRchfOfLxY2). Candidates who do not apply through the online scholarship form will not be considered.
- **Scholarship decisions will be communicated in June 2026.**
- Both part-time and full-time students are eligible to apply. Home/EU and Overseas/Islands applicants are eligible to apply. However, scholarship funds cover the amount of Home/EU tuition fees only for any successful awardee and applicants would be required to pay the difference towards any remaining fees.
- Imperial policy dictates that students can only hold multiple awards if one is for fees and the other is a stipend. As the School of Public Health Master's Scholarships provide an award for fees, recipients would be permitted to also hold an award for a stipend, but will not be permitted to hold more than one full scholarship.
- Applicants are welcome to apply for other types of funding from Imperial while applying for a School of Public Health Masters Scholarship. However, these scholarships cannot be combined with any other scholarship that covers fees.

Multiple Applications.content:
- You can apply for **up to two courses** in an academic year, only one of which can be for Imperial Business School.
- If you are applying for two courses you should submit only one application, listing your course preferences, rather than submitting two separate applications.
- You should list your preferred course as your first choice and your reserve course as your second choice as we will consider your application for courses in the order they are submitted.
- We will only consider your second choice if your first-choice application is unsuccessful.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Under exceptional circumstances, you may apply to defer your admission to the **next academic year**. Deferral requests are based on a change of circumstance that is outside your control and could not have been foreseen, and that will prevent you from taking up your place on the original course start date. Deferral requests are granted or denied at the discretion of academic departments.
To request a deferral, contact the relevant [admissions team](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/apply/contact/) outlining your circumstances and reasons for your request.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you have received a conditional offer, it will include the conditions you need to meet before Imperial can confirm your place. This may include providing evidence of your academic qualifications and [proficiency in English language](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/apply/english-language/). You will need to satisfy **all the conditions listed in your offer before you can register at Imperial**.
- As part of your offer conditions, Imperial may ask you to provide evidence of your academic qualifications, such as your degree transcript. Imperial works with Qualification Check to verify academic qualifications, accessible via the link included in your offer conditions.
- If you take IELTS, IELTS Indicator, TOEFL, Pearson, Cambridge Advanced/Proficiency, or Duolingo English to meet your English language offer condition, Imperial needs to verify your test results online.
- Certain courses at Imperial require students to obtain [Academic Technology Approval Scheme (ATAS)](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/academic-technology-approval-scheme) clearance as part of the entry requirements. If this applies to you, it will be included in your offer conditions. You will need to request an ATAS certificate before you apply for your student visa.
